economicActivity.label: Economic activity Google helped provide
economicActivity.definition: Google's own estimate of the economic activity that Google Search, Google Ads, Google Cloud, AdSense/AdMob, Ad Grants, YouTube and Google Play helped provide for a state's businesses, nonprofits, publishers, creators and developers. Modeled by the Google Economics team (e.g. $8 of profit per $1 of Google Ads spend), not measured output, not GDP and not Google's own spending. States reported in millions are converted to billions (shown in square brackets in the quote).

businesses.label: Businesses using Google's free tools
businesses.definition: Businesses in the state that "used Google's tools at no cost to receive phone calls, bookings, reviews, requests for directions, or other direct connections to their customers". Always reported as "more than".

investment.label: Cumulative Google investment in the state
investment.period: cumulative, from the year the state's first data center was built through the 2025 report
investment.definition: Google's statement that it "has invested more than" (Georgia: "has committed more than ... of investment") the amount in the state since its data center(s) there were built. The 2025 report says "Investment methodology now reflects total data center investment (construction, server and networking infrastructure)", so these figures are on a broader basis than the 2024 edition's and are not comparable with it. Reported only for the 13 states with Google data centers; cumulative, not annual.

longLivedAssets.label: Long-lived assets
longLivedAssets.definition: Property and equipment, net, plus operating lease assets, by geographic area (10-K Note 15). Columns are 2024 then 2025; the 2025 value is recorded.

notes: Source: Google's own 2024 U.S. Economic Impact Report (national PDF with one page per state, data for calendar 2024, PDF created April 2025), the edition matching the Dec 2024 snapshot. The live site economicimpact.google now shows the 2025 edition (published April 2026, higher figures); not used. Methodology page credits the Google Economics team and its own multipliers (Hal Varian's $2 profit per $1 ad spend, organic-click adjustment), so tier is company-published, not commissioned, but the economic-activity figures are model estimates of value to other businesses, not Google spending. 50 states + DC have economic activity and business counts; Puerto Rico has a page too ($269 million, 141,000+ businesses) but is not a state, so it is left out. Investment figures exist only for the 13 states with data centers and are cumulative since each data center was built. The report also gives philanthropic giving, volunteer hours and Ad Grants by state; not recorded. Google publishes no employees-by-state figures here (nationally: more than 100,000 U.S. full-time employees, offices and data centers in 26 states). The 10-K gives no property breakdown by state or country, so sites are the HQ (10-K) plus 11 data centers as described on the state pages. No employee, office or tax breakdown by country was found; the only geographic split of physical footprint in the 10-K is long-lived assets (property and equipment plus operating lease assets), United States vs International, recorded as one country row and one region row. Google's data-center locations page (google.com/about/datacenters/locations) and office list (about.google/locations) were checked: both are current (2026) lists of places with no figures, so they add nothing countable; the data-center sites above use the 2024 report's own wording. Tier basis: the 2024 PDF's methodology is written in Google's voice ("Our first chief economist, Hal Varian"), with no outside author named.
